notes: The SHORT, on the v2 plate kit. Every `plate` here is a registry key and
every `bind` target is a slot that plate DECLARES — the renderer puts the
text in the slot and does nothing else. Type is set in the face, size,
weight and colour role the kit declares for that slot's role, so the
character budgets are the kit's own `maxChars` rather than something
measured by running a fitter over this file.
THE VERTICAL SET IS TEN FAMILIES, NOT THE WHOLE KIT. The comps table, the
scatter, the waterfall, the grouped bars, the flow plate and the diff
plate are 16:9 by design: they need horizontal room to be readable and
they do not belong in seventy-five seconds. Nothing here reaches for one.
Positions and type sizes are fractions of FRAME HEIGHT, so one template
holds at any delivery resolution. Large type and the caption band never
coexist: a shot carrying type at 6.5% of frame height or more sets
captions false, and the parser refuses the template if it does not.
THE HOST IS IN FOUR SHOTS AND THE CLOSE-UP CARRIES THE TURN. He was in the
cold open, the payoff and the close, all three at full figure in a wide
room — which is the shot you use when the room is the point. The turn is
the line the whole cut rests on and it was being told on bare ground with
nobody in it. `host/close-up` is head and shoulders and it exists for
exactly that beat.

A STATIC PLATE MAY HOLD. The ceiling was written when every plate in the kit boiled; 44 of the 140 are `playback: static` now, because a figure that moves is a figure being re-read. What keeps a data beat short is the ceiling itself, and it is set to what a seventy-second cut of ten beats actually gives each one.

ALTERNATES: a beat may name other plates that can carry it, and code picks between them, rotating off what the last few videos used. The writer still chooses nothing — that is the point of a format that exists to be mass-produced. An alternate restates `bind` when it names its slots differently, and inherits when it does not.

ORDERS: an alternate sequence may only move shots the NARRATION does not pin. A shot with an `anchor` starts where its own words are spoken, and the words are one take written to the beat order in the writing prompt, so moving an anchored beat puts the picture over the wrong sentence. Only unanchored shots, and ones sharing an anchor with another, are free — which today is one swap. Reordering beats properly means the prompt stating the order it picked and the script carrying it back.

THE ROUND-ONE PHONE PLATES that a short script can fill are alternates here: the fifth hook card, the move on the day in both directions, and the one-line close. Placing a figure the size of the move's on a shot with captions switches the captions off for that shot, in code, because the template's `captions` flag cannot know which plate the rotation will pick.

shots.notes: The hook card is the format's own opener — three treatments, and which one a video gets is a property of the script, not of this file.

alts.notes: Same three slots, a different treatment.
The third treatment. `huge` goes unfilled, which is the drawing, not a gap.

The fifth treatment: the hook on a full field with the ticker at the foot, so the eye lands on the sentence before the chip. The same three slots. `hook-card-t4` is not here on purpose — it leads with the figure at 240pt, and the next beat is that figure.

shots.notes: The price, as a path through the figures the data carries. `plot-area` is a data region: it takes the series and the renderer draws it, which is not the renderer computing anything — it is being handed one.

alts.notes: THE MOVE AS ONE FIGURE, WITH ITS ARROW. The arrow is drawn, so the plate has to match the sign: `chart.move_up` is the move summary's leading figure only when it opens on a `+`, and nothing otherwise, which makes this plate ineligible on a fall. The rest of the summary is the label. It needs no price data, so a short rendered without prices still has a picture for this beat. The session path the plate reserves room for stays empty: the price data is daily closes, and six of those in a box drawn for one session would read as a day.
The falling twin, eligible only on a move summary that opens on a minus.

shots.notes: A headline on paper, in the band drawn for it. Three treatments exist so two headlines in one video are not the same picture twice.

alts.notes: NEWS-RELEASE ART, AND THE SCRIPT ALREADY CARRIES IT. A script may declare three headlines and the band shows one, so the other two were written and never drawn. `headline-2` is bound REQUIRED on purpose: a stack of three with two empty rows is a broken drawing rather than a sparse one, so the rotation only reaches for this when the writer actually filed a second headline.

shots.notes: The line the cut rests on, told to camera in close-up. Allowed to be empty — a video with no turn drops this shot rather than holding an empty frame. The room is a ROLE, not a key: three angles fill `talk` and which one a video gets is its seed's, so the channel's shorts are not all shot from the same chair.

One row per shot: the band lights and the frame moves to it. Steps that differ only by which row carries a rectangle are one shot with extra runtime — but a vertical sheet's row is already the width of the frame, so the move is a pan rather than a zoom past the figures. No host: there is no room for a figure in front of a wall-sized sheet, and he returns at the payoff.

alts.notes: The same sheet with a sparkline column. `head-spark` is the kit's own label and takes no binding.
A taller sheet: three rows lit against five bands rather than three.

shots.notes: Pull back: every row up at once, after the walk down them.
What the sheet meant, in the plate drawn for a line worth pulling out. The numbers comment is written at two hundred characters and there is nowhere on a sheet to put one.

alts.notes: The read as a term and its meaning. `definition` names its slots nothing like `quote-pull`, so it restates the binds.

shots.notes: Two things that are both true at once. The plate the format opens on more than any other.
The one figure the video is about, at the size it deserves.
Resigned, not conclusive. The handle sits under it where the date label goes.

alts.notes: THE OTHER WAY TO END. All three vertical formats closed on `structure/closing` every time, so every short in the channel signed off on the same drawing. The conclusion is a line worth pulling out by definition, and `quote-pull`'s body is the only other 9:16 plate wide enough to hold one without narrowing what the writer may write — `structure/end-card` holds 58 characters against closing's 136, so rotating onto it would have shrunk every conclusion in the channel to suit the alternate.

ONE THING AT STATEMENT SIZE. The original close has three lines and a script has one conclusion, so two of them were always empty. The handle moves up to the kicker: this plate's date label sits inside the caption band, where the last spoken words would run over it. Its detail line stays empty — the plate's own caution is not to pad it.

orders.name: comment-first
orders.notes: The read before the pull-back instead of after it. `the-sheet` and `the-comment` both listen for `numbers_comment`, so the voice does not care which lands first — which is what makes this the one swap the narration leaves free.
